title: The Corner Watch
one_line_concept: Aachu and Zuv keep saving each other from the same sharp table corner without ever turning it into a romantic speech.
emotional_truth: Love is sometimes just a hand appearing between your head and the furniture before you even notice danger.
relatable_trigger: Couples who live around the same tables, shelves, bed corners, and tiny household hazards recognize the automatic palm-on-corner reflex.
share_trigger: Send to the partner who silently protects your head from furniture like it is their unpaid job.
suggested_hook_text: love is a hand on the sharp corner.
visual_evidence: A repeated mutual gesture: one bends near the same table corner and the other covers it with a hand; later the roles reverse; final slide shows the hand arriving before the bump.
slide_count_reason: Three slides can work, but four gives the repeated mutual behavior enough rhythm without overexplaining it.
why_it_wins: Most emotionally original behavior in the room.
Mutual care without gendered incompetence or saint/fool framing.
Fresh and not a repeat of the previous shortlist.
Simple prop world: one table corner, one hand, readable faces.

risks.mitigation: Use one table corner, one shelf/bedside corner, and role reversal to create rhythm.

risks.risk: If staged too softly, it could become generic care.
risks.mitigation: Make the hand-on-corner gesture the hero proof in every beat.
